answer_1.quote: The automatic generation of evidence-supported CS has been extensively researched.

answer_2.quote: To evaluate the factuality and faithfulness of the generated CS, We follow the evaluation from [citation] we use four metrics which are factuality (FA), faithfulness to Hate Speech (FH), faithfulness to Claim (FC) and faithfulness for Evidence (FE), and Diversity (D).

answer_3.quote: We employ an LM-based factuality checker, denoted as Ckr(•) to calculate the likelihood of entailment for each evidence-triplet pair.

answer_4.quote: In human evaluation, we randomly sample 100 CS generated by GPT-3.5 and Llama3 from the CONAN dataset. Given the HS, claim, evidence, and the generated CS, we recruit five annotators (majority rule) to assign a score from 1 to 5 (1: not at all, 3: OK, 5: very good) to the generated CS based on the aspects of factuality, faithfulness for HS, claim and evidence.
answer_4.guideline: Assign a score from 1 to 5 for factuality, faithfulness to hate speech, faithfulness to claim, and faithfulness to evidence.
